body:
As we redefined levels with a goal to have an easier entry level, there is a need to review levels for requirements to match that direction.

It has taken quite some time and effort, but with Josh, we went through the issues and had many discussions over changes and matching the new direction.

Do not throw everything out all at once and provide it in a more readable, manageable, and discussable way, I'll open an issue per chapter to cover (only) requirements with level changes.

Note, that level changes are compared to current requirements in bleeding edge version (not compared to release v4.0.3) and level changes in modification tags (e.g. 'LEVEL L1 > L2') may not be up to date anymore.

Level changes are written in format "`<from current level> > <to new level>`", e.g. if current level was 1 and it is changed to level 3, then it is marked as `1 > 3`.

Level definitions in the document are waiting for some updates as well.
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x03-Using-ASVS.md

The rough principles to keep in mind when analyzing levels:

  * Level 1 - the first step in
    * Really-really must have, without that you can not be secure
    * First layer of defense - if this is the only requirement not satisfied in the application, you still have a usable security hole (it means - no preconditions)
  * Level 2 - the basic level
    * Expected basic security level that every application should achieve
    * May contain "first layer of defense" requirements for "not that widespread" problems or complicated to attack scenarios that are moved away from the "first priority" list
  * Level 3 - an extra step
    * Defense in depth
    * Advanced level (financial, healthcare)

---

Update: where seems to be agreement and/or no discussion going on, those level updates are merged in to move fast forward. If there is need to update or discuss any requirement or level, it is always possible to open a separate issue to address that.

comments.body: I think these principles are reasonable. Can you expand on them a bit more? What is Midground vs. Advanced/Niche?

I updated definitions a bit and added an explanation line
> Level changes are written in format "<from current level> > <to new level>", e.g. if current level was 1 and it is changed to level 3, then it is marked as 1 > 3.

Ok, another round of level-reviews (almost) done - thanks a lot to @randomstuff and @jmanico for high-pace feedback.

V6 not yet merged and ~8 more requirements are in process to be added, current numbers are:
* L1 - 73 requirements
* L2 - 175 requirements
* L3 - 97 requirements

(Total 345 requirements)

The next step from here is a "justification round" - does everything fit the level together with other requirements on the same level or somethings is outlined?

For "grouped by level" I have one extra view available:
https://asvs.dev/levels_v5.0.be.html
We can consider this round of level changes done, previous comment stays valid, but I'll close this issue now as there is no action to be expected from this anymore.
